local_mode_caveat: Local-terminal mode: the approval was typed at a terminal on the user's own machine by approve_local.py, committed and pushed by the user, and imported here; import read the commit, its author and committer and the file stored in it with read-only git queries, and wrote an import record that must be committed and pushed before any BCA run. Nothing in this session typed or wrote the user's file. It still cannot prove who typed it: approve_local.py checks only that standard input is a terminal, and git's author and committer fields are set by whoever makes the commit and are not authenticated, so anyone able to push to the repository, an agent with push access included, could make such a commit under the user's name; an agent could also write this runs-side file by hand. The added strength holds only if the user checks on GitHub that the commit the import record names is the user's own.
